fact: Antananarivo's urban commune launched digitalisation of its markets on 7 October 2026: traders are registered on tablets, issued chip-and-QR merchant cards loaded with funds, and commune agents debit dues on payment terminals each day, replacing paper tickets and receipts.
The article describes only the Commune Urbaine d'Antananarivo launching the system, with the first merchant cards distributed on 7 October 2026; it names no other commune.

The commune's market digitalisation was launched on 7 October 2026, with first cards distributed that day; markets are the commune's third revenue source at 7 to 9 billion ariary a year, per its finance director.
UNDP states the G-IFPB software, fed by a 2019 taxpayer census, was handed over on 2021-09-13 to manage collection of the built-property tax in Toamasina.
The software was installed at the Commune Urbaine de Toamasina and at the Direction Régionale des Impôts Atsinanana, per UNDP.
Only Toamasina commune uses G-IFPB; UNDP says staff were trained to replicate the process in the city's other arrondissements, and communes later equipped may use it.
UNDP, through its GBCI project with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, supported and developed the software and installed it.
UNDP reports the software's operational launch and official handover in Toamasina on 2021-09-13 (outside the last twelve months of the study date).
